key_insight: In localized nonorthogonal flow representations, Reynolds stress arises from coupled velocity fluctuations rather than additive energies of separately labeled structures.
engineering_relevance: Structure-based turbulence diagnostics must retain cross covariance and quantify velocity-span overlap to avoid misleading momentum-flux attribution.
method: Represent JHTDB homogeneous isotropic turbulence with frozen, curl-lifted anisotropic Gaussian vorticity functions.
Map coefficient covariance to represented velocity stress through a fixed Biot–Savart map.
Analyze principal-angle overlap and cross covariance, then compare orthogonal Fourier and POD regroupings.
evidence_signal: At a principal-cosine threshold of 0.95, 55% of sheet-associated directions overlap closely with tube-like directions; shared-direction products carry 99.6% of covariance cancellation, and removing between-family covariance increases DNS-referenced stress error by factors of 53.6–87.
watch_item: Morphology labels and stress attribution remain representation-dependent; results should not be interpreted as unique physical contributions from sheets or tubes.
paper_title: Identifiability Limits of Reynolds-Stress Attribution in Localized Nonorthogonal Flow Representations
